notes.sample_point: Interior representative point of the largest polygon of each LGA. A geometric centroid can fall in the bay for coastal councils.

sources.name: Open-Meteo forecast API
sources.coverage: Daily temperature at one interior point in each Victorian LGA, 2026-10-31 to 2026-11-14
sources.notes: No API key. Upstream weather models via Open-Meteo.

sources.name: Open-Meteo historical weather API (ERA5)
sources.coverage: Daily temperature, 2016-01-01 to 2026-10-30, one interior point per Victorian LGA
sources.notes: ERA5 reanalysis lags the present by several days, so the archive end date is the last day the API returned.

sources.name: Open-Meteo air quality API (CAMS)
sources.coverage: Hourly PM2.5 and ozone, aggregated to local days, next 5 days, one point per Victorian LGA
sources.notes: Smoke is not a separate field. Fine-particle pollution (PM2.5) is the smoke proxy. EPA Victoria's keyed API is not used.

sources.name: ABS ASGS 2021 Local Government Areas
sources.coverage: Victorian LGA boundaries, generalised for the map, GDA2020 via Web Mercator query returned in WGS84
sources.notes: Geometry simplified with maxAllowableOffset 0.008 degrees for the dashboard.

sources.name: ABS Census 2021 General Community Profile G01
sources.coverage: Usual-resident population, children aged 0-4, and ages 65-74, 75-84 and 85+ by Victorian LGA
sources.notes: Small random adjustments are applied by the ABS to protect privacy.

sources.name: ABS Data by Region, income, 2021
sources.coverage: Median equivalised household income and the share of households under $500 a week, Victorian LGAs

sources.name: ABS Data by Region, family and community, 2021
sources.coverage: Lone-person households and total households by Victorian LGA
sources.notes: Table field hhtype_22021 is lone-person households.

sources.name: Victorian heat-health temperature thresholds
sources.licence: Public government page, cited; not a bulk download
sources.coverage: District thresholds 30, 32 and 34°C and the council-to-district list
sources.notes: Used only as the published temperature cut-offs. No health-outcome microdata.
